name: chicken pot pie
instructions:
Poached-and-shredded chicken breast in a leek-carrot-celery rosemary gravy, filled into a pie with a real pastry top.

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. POACH THE CHICKEN: poach shreddable chicken breast in chicken broth with a BAY LEAF. BEST METHOD: a COVERED GLASS CASSEROLE DISH AT 325°F — easiest to control. (Instapot alternative: chip it up, knee-deep in braising liquid, LOW PRESSURE for 5 MINUTES — low pressure gets cooking faster and the chicken doesn't sit in boiling water as long.) Keep the poaching stock — it becomes the gravy liquid.
2. SAUTÉ THE VEGETABLES: in a big frying pan, sauté leeks + carrots + celery + garlic + rosemary + a BAY LEAF in a MIX OF BUTTER AND OLIVE OIL, with ONION POWDER (the onion powder + leek combo — same move as the chicken soup version, [[french-chicken-soup]]). SKIP THE THYME; rosemary is the herb (see notes). Herbes de provence are clashing.
3. FLOUR WHEN THE LIQUID GOES AWAY: add flour once the pan liquid has cooked off. Stir well so all the vegetables are covered and NO WHITE FLOUR is visible.
4. CREAM FIRST, THEN STOCK: the cream goes in BEFORE the stock and gets some heat to bring out its flavor. Then pour in the chicken stock you poached the breast in, plus more to fill the pot, with a LITTLE CHICKEN BOUILLON for a boost — controlled amount (see notes).
5. STEW COVERED until the carrots are cooked, then UNCOVER until it becomes a thick gravy.
6. BEURRE MANIE to thicken further, until desired.
7. PEAS AND POTATOES TOWARD THE END: both work well, but add them late. Peas are low risk; potatoes can get overcooked or undercooked easily — FINELY DICE them so they're predictable.
8. DIJON MUSTARD LATE for tang (primary — see notes).
9. CHICKEN IN AT THE END: shred and add the poached breast last, then fill the pie.
10. TOP AND BAKE: a REAL PIE TOP is ideal for this recipe. THE TOP: [[olive-oil-pie-crust]] — it bakes well and is easy to spread on top. If there's a BASE crust, butter/lard ([[butter-pie-crust]]) is probably better there — the flavorful base (see notes). Gratining with breadcrumbs + spray oil is a good option too — use DEVILED BREADCRUMBS, superior to regular breadcrumbs here (see notes).
notes:
=== ROSEMARY IS THE HERB — CONFIRMED AGAINST THE CHICKEN ITSELF ===

ROSEMARY confirmed to pair well with THE CHICKEN MEAT ITSELF in the dense pie — not just the gravy around it. A BAY LEAF goes in alongside it (in the sauté, in addition to the one in the poach). ROSEMARY, BAY LEAF, AND MUSTARD ARE ENOUGH — it doesn't need SAGE or HERBES DE PROVENCE (both clashing). SKIP THE THYME. JULIA CHILD OPTS FOR TARRAGON AND PARSLEY — I skip both; PARSLEY is CLASHING.

=== POACH — COVERED GLASS CASSEROLE AT 325°F IS BEST ===

A COVERED GLASS CASSEROLE DISH AT 325°F is the best poaching method — easiest to control. Chicken in broth with a bay leaf; the poaching liquid double-dips as the gravy stock. The instapot route (LOW pressure, 5 minutes, knee-deep in broth) remains the alternative — low pressure gets cooking faster and is gentler on the breast, which needs to stay shreddable, not rubbery.

=== STOCK — REAL CHICKEN STOCK PLUS A LITTLE BOUILLON BOOST ===

Real chicken stock (the perishable kind) is good here — and a LITTLE CHICKEN BOUILLON is also NEEDED for a boost, in a CONTROLLED AMOUNT. The boost on top of real stock, not bouillon instead of stock.

=== THE GRAVY BUILD — FLOUR ON THE VEGETABLES, THEN CREAM, THEN STOCK ===

The flour goes on the sautéed vegetables once their liquid has cooked off — stirred until no white flour is visible — before any liquid goes in (roux-on-the-vegetables, not a separate roux). Then CREAM FIRST — it gets some heat to bring out its flavor — then the poaching stock + more stock + the bouillon boost. Covered until the carrots are done, uncovered to reduce to a thick gravy, and a beurre manie to close the gap to the thickness you want.

=== ONION POWDER + LEEK ===

Onion powder joins the sauté — the ONION POWDER + LEEK combo, the same move as the chicken soup version of this dish ([[french-chicken-soup]]).

=== PEAS BELONG HERE ===

Peas work well in a pot pie specifically because all the resulting gravy is consumed inside the pie — no broth is left behind on the plate, no bowl-bottom puddle. Peas are small enough to be eaten alongside the other components in every bite, they add an earthy vegetal note that the cream-rosemary-chicken base doesn't otherwise carry, and they bring more protein. They're not a standard chicken-stew addition (in a fricassee they'd get lost in a deep bowl of sauce), but the pot-pie format makes them earn their place. Add toward the end — low risk.

=== POTATOES FOR STARCH WITHOUT MSG GUMMINESS — FINELY DICED, ADDED LATE ===

Potatoes add starchy body that thickens the final filling and gives it more chew. This matters because the alternative — pushing the gravy thicker with more bouillon/MSG or more flour — leaves the filling gummy and one-note. Potatoes do the thickening structurally instead of chemically; the dish reads richer without reading artificial. They're the risky late addition though: easy to overcook or undercook — FINELY DICE them so they're predictable.

=== DIJON — PRIMARY, ADDED LATE, FOR TANG ===

Dijon mustard is PRIMARY — added LATE, for TANG. (Promoted from its old secondary only-with-potatoes status.)

=== FINELY CHOPPED, NOT PROCESSED — BITE-SIZED FOR THE GRAVY ===

Every component (leeks, celery, carrots, potatoes, chicken) should be finely chopped but kept bite-sized — not pulverized in a food processor. The goal is a cohesive gravy solution where each forkful has a bit of everything in it. Knife-and-cutting-board instincts are right here. Processor-fine vegetables dissolve into the cream base and lose textural identity; large rustic-chunk cuts leave you fishing for specific components rather than eating a unified bite. Aim for the size that survives the bake but disappears against the others on the fork.

=== IT'S A PIE, NOT A STEW — DON'T LET STEW INSTINCTS SEASON IT ===

It NEEDS A CRUST, and the crust is A LOT OF THE FLAVOR. It's easy to OVER-SEASON with any ingredient, and to UNDER-FLOUR or UNDER-CREAM, because your stew instincts can kick in — but this is a PIE, and the final form tastes different than a stew.

=== TOP — REAL PIE CRUST FIRST; OLIVE OIL CRUST FOR THE TOP, BUTTER/LARD FOR A BASE ===

A real pastry pie top is ideal for this recipe. THE CRUST SPLIT: I personally love the [[olive-oil-pie-crust]] as the TOP — it bakes well and is easy to spread on top. BUTTER/LARD ([[butter-pie-crust]]) is probably better for the flavorful BASE.

The breadcrumb + spray-oil gratin is a good option too — and DEVILED BREADCRUMBS are the pick there, superior to regular breadcrumbs.
